Uomo di 61 anni con melanoma. PET-TC con: 61-year-old man with melanoma. Follow-up 18F-FDG PET-CT (skull base to thighs), about 5 months after the prior PET-CT; contrast-enhanced CT. Interim therapies not indicated by the collection. The images and the report of the prior PET-CT are available.

Nel controllo oncologico con PET-TC si p:
In oncologic follow-up with PET-CT, you start from the prior report and images: every known lesion is found again and measured (diameters on CT, SUV on PET), and then new lesions are sought throughout the field of view. New lesions define progression both by RECIST 1.1 (CT) and by PERCIST/EORTC (PET), even if other lesions improve.

Here the two small lesions of the prior exam have grown considerably (left external iliac lymph node and right abdominal lesion anterior to the kidney: in melanoma they may be lymph nodes, but also bowel or mesenteric metastases) and new lesions appear, including a right supraclavicular lymph node: metabolic progression.

Uptake not to be confused with disease: brown fat (in the prior exam), vocal cords, bowel, urinary tract. Also try the lesion followed over time: measure the volume of the iliac lesion in the two exams and look at the doubling time.
Controllo oncologico: ritrova ogni lesio: Oncologic follow-up: find again every lesion in the prior report, then look for new ones. A new lesion is progression.

Whole-body 18F-FDG PET-CT (about 270 MBq, acquisition about 60 minutes after injection); contrast-enhanced CT. Weight 66 kg.

Small hypermetabolic focus in the right abdomen, anterior to the right kidney, to be attributed to a lymph node or a bowel localization. Small hypermetabolic left external iliac lymph node. Symmetric uptake in supraclavicular and thoracic paravertebral fat: brown fat. Physiologic vocal cord uptake; urinary excretion.

Conclusions: two small foci suspicious for melanoma localizations (right abdomen, left external iliac lymph node). Close follow-up is recommended.
